encounters.cc: Follow-up appointment after recent pulmonary function testing

lines: Follow-up appointment after recent pulmonary function testing
He reports gradually worsening shortness of breath over the past year, which he initially attributed to aging.
He now finds it difficult to walk several blocks without stopping to catch his breath.
He denies cough or sputum production but admits to occasionally using his wife’s albuterol inhaler for relief.
He has an 80-pack-year history of cigarette smoking and quit only recently.
Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds bilaterally and hyperresonance to percussion.
The chest wall has increased anteroposterior diameter, and accessory muscle use is noted during quiet breathing.
Cardiopulmonary examination reveals a loud P2.
Pulmonary function tests show a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio of 55%.
Total lung capacity and residual volume are both elevated.

The patient is a 55-year-old male with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, peripheral artery disease, and severe upper lobe predominant emphysema who presents with progressively worsening hypertension following his January 2020 pulmonary evaluation.
He has a 12-year history of well-controlled high blood pressure managed with hydrochlorothiazide.
However, over the past 6 months, his systolic blood pressure has increased to 180–190 mm Hg, requiring the recent addition of a second antihypertensive agent.
His medical history includes smoking and peripheral artery disease.
He underwent a femoral artery stent placement 2 years ago

encounters.cc: Progressive dyspnea, hoarseness, and a cough

lines: Progressive dyspnea, hoarseness, and a cough
The patient returns to Pulmonary and Critical Care with severe upper lobe predominant emphysema and presents with a 3-month history of progressive dyspnea, hoarseness, and a cough.
He denies any fever, weight loss, or night sweats.
His medical history is significant for hypertension.
On physical examination, you note stridor that is present both during inspiration and expiration.
His voice is raspy, and there is no palpable lymphadenopathy.
Pulmonary function tests reveal a flow-volume loop with flattening of both the inspiratory and expiratory limbs.

encounters.cc: Progressive fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion

lines: Progressive fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion

This 57-year-old male with severe upper lobe predominant emphysema and recent evaluation for tracheal pathology presents to the Hematology and Oncology clinic with a 3-month history of progressive fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion.
He reports a 10-pound unintentional weight loss over the same period but denies any fever, night sweats, or changes in bowel habits.
His past medical history is significant for hypertension.
On physical examination, he appears pale and has conjunctival pallor.

encounters.cc: Chronic cough and recent weight loss

lines: Chronic cough and recent weight loss
The patient with severe emphysema returns for chronic cough and weight loss, reporting a cough productive of yellowish sputum for the past 3 months and denying fever, night sweats, or hemoptysis.
His blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute.
Physical examination reveals decreased breath sounds and dullness to percussion at the right lung base.
Chest X-ray shows a mass in the right lower lobe.
Histopathology confirms non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
A case-control study is initiated to identify potential risk factors for NSCLC.
Researchers select 100 patients with newly diagnosed NSCLC as cases and 100 age-matched controls without lung cancer from the same geographic area.
They collect data on smoking history, occupational exposures, and family history of cancer.
The patient is referred to a pulmonologist who performs a bronchoscopy and biopsies the mass.

encounters.cc: Intermittent, dull abdominal pain over the past 3 months

lines: Intermittent, dull abdominal pain over the past 3 months
This patient with Stage IIIB lung cancer presents with abdominal pain.
The pain is poorly localized, occurs more often after meals, and occasionally radiates to the back.
- Stage IIIB Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
His medical history includes hypertension and hyperlipidemia.
He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years.
He has no nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or hematochezia.
Physical examination reveals a pulsatile mass in the central abdomen without tenderness.
Abdominal CT angiography demonstrates a saccular aneurysm arising from the proximal superior mesenteric artery just distal to its origin from the aorta.
The aneurysm measures 3.8 cm in diameter and projects posteriorly.

His wife reports that he has had a persistent headache for the past two weeks, which has not improved with over-the-counter analgesics.
She also mentions that he has been increasingly forgetful and had difficulty finding words during conversations.

On examination, the patient is postictal but has no evident focal neurologic deficits.
An MRI of the brain is performed and reveals multiple, well-circumscribed lesions at the gray and white matter junction with surrounding vasogenic edema.
